suitability_reason: Every decided issue turns on credibility, dominion-and-control/nominee fact-finding, substantiation, or reasonable cause; no mechanically computable issue remains (the 6662 threshold was met but the penalty was removed on reasonable cause).

taxpayer.notes: Filed Form 1040-SR as 'retired'; graduated high school 1965; long-time cafeteria manager. Schedule C for Broward Parking tow-truck business operated in practice by her daughter's then-partner Mr. Becker.

adjustments: disallowed Schedule C expenses of $103,986 (all except $1,500 supplies) for lack of substantiation
$17,984 of Social Security benefits determined taxable
self-employment tax of $10,526 (offset by $5,263 SE/AGI adjustment)
qualified business income deduction of $13,846 allowed under section 199A
section 6662(a) penalty for negligence or substantial understatement
notice_of_deficiency.contested_by_taxpayer: Taxability of Schedule C income (nominee theory, duress); no error assigned to disallowed deductions; penalty

findings_of_fact.fact: BoA account opened October 19, 2018 in name 'Maureen F. Shoe, Sole Prop, d/b/a Broward Parking'; petitioner sole signatory
findings_of_fact.snippet: Petitioner was the only person with signatory authority over this ac- count.

findings_of_fact.fact: 209 deposits in 2019 totaling $74,983, all Broward Parking receipts; opening balance $9,053 at January 1, 2019
findings_of_fact.snippet: During 2019 there were 209 deposits into the BoA account, all reflecting Broward Parking receipts.

findings_of_fact.fact: Petitioner used the account: $896 IRS payment April 15, 2019; checks of $75 (preparer) and $376 (cash); $20,000 cash withdrawal September 6, 2019 for engagement ring
findings_of_fact.snippet: The only other activity on the BoA account during 2019 was a $20,000 cash withdrawal on September 6, 2019.

findings_of_fact.fact: Closing balance December 31, 2019 of $51,709, petitioner sole person authorized; testimony that she did not know what happened to funds not credible
findings_of_fact.snippet: On December 31, 2019, the BoA account showed a closing balance of $51,709.

findings_of_fact.fact: 2019 return: wages $26,787, taxable retirement income $1,949, Social Security $21,158 (taxable portion reported zero), business loss $29,493, standard deduction $13,850, AGI negative $14,607, withholding $2,664 claimed as refund
findings_of_fact.snippet: On this return petitioner reported wages of $26,787, taxable re- tirement income of $1,949, and Social Security benefits of $21,158,

findings_of_fact.fact: Schedule C gross receipts $75,993; expenses $105,486: car/truck $27,086, legal/professional $62,700, supplies $1,500, other $14,200 ($1,200 telephone, $13,000 signs)
findings_of_fact.snippet: On Schedule C petitioner reported gross receipts of $75,993 from Broward Parking.

findings_of_fact.fact: No substantiating documents introduced at trial; no error assigned to disallowance
findings_of_fact.snippet: Petitioner did not seek to introduce these receipts (or any other substantiating documents) into evidence at trial.

findings_of_fact.fact: Return reported overpayment of $2,664; deficiency $25,887 sustained; understatement exceeded $5,000 and 10% of tax required to be shown
findings_of_fact.snippet: Petitioner’s understatement of income tax thus exceeded $5,000 and 10% of the tax required to be shown on her return.

findings_of_fact.fact: Civil penalty approval form signed by Group Manager on August 20, 2021
findings_of_fact.snippet: which Group Manager Anthony DeCarvalho signed on August 20, 2021.

findings_of_fact.fact: No tax law knowledge; return professionally prepared with information supplied by Mr. Becker
findings_of_fact.snippet: Petitioner has no knowledge of tax law and has spent most of her adult life as a cafeteria manager.

issues.question: Must petitioner include the Broward Parking Schedule C gross receipts in 2019 income, or was she a mere nominee acting under duress?
issues.holding: Included; she had complete dominion and control over the BoA account; nominee and duress arguments rejected
issues.computable_reason: Turns on dominion-and-control/nominee fact-finding and credibility

issues.question: Other (Schedule C business expense deductions §162/§274(d)): Is petitioner entitled to the disallowed Schedule C deductions of $103,986?
issues.holding: No; no substantiating evidence offered and no basis for Cohan estimate

issues.question: Is petitioner liable for the $5,177 section 6662(a) accuracy-related penalty?
issues.holding: No; although understatement was substantial and approval was timely, she had reasonable cause and acted in good faith

amount_determined.description: penalty determined in notice, not sustained

issues.computable_reason: Decided on reasonable cause and good faith (§6664(c)(1))

decision.text: Decision will be entered for respondent as to the deficiency and for petitioner as to the accuracy-related penalty.
decision.summary: Deficiency of $25,887 sustained; section 6662(a) penalty not imposed (reasonable cause)

notes: Court notes $75,993 reported receipts exceed 2019 deposits ($74,983) by $1,010, unresolved. Social Security taxability ($17,984) and SE tax ($10,526) are computational consequences, not separately contested. Some snippets preserve PDF hyphenation ('ac- count', 're- tirement').
